root_cause.text: In mm/huge_memory.c, __split_huge_pmd_locked() used the folio after dropping its last reference by calling mm_counter_file(folio) after folio_put(), creating a use-after-free on folio state.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says the file/shmem RSS counter was updated “after dropping the PMD mapping's folio reference” and that if folio_put() drops the last reference, mm_counter_file() “can later read freed folio state via folio_test_swapbacked()”; the patch fixes this by moving add_mm_counter(mm, mm_counter_file(folio), -HPAGE_PMD_NR) before folio_put(folio).

agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message explicitly says the file/shmem RSS counter was updated “after dropping the PMD mapping's folio reference” and that if folio_put() drops the last reference, mm_counter_file() “can later read freed folio state via folio_test_swapbacked()”; the patch fixes this by moving add_mm_counter(mm, mm_counter_file(folio), -HPAGE_PMD_NR) before folio_put(folio).

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix an early-exit path in huge PMD splitting to decrement MM counters before releasing the folio and returning.
intent_record.what: In `__split_huge_pmd_locked`, within the branch that checks `if (folio != page_folio(page))`, the change adds a call to `add_mm_counter(mm, mm_counter_file(folio), -HPAGE_PMD_NR);` immediately before `folio_put(folio);` and also adds an explicit `return;` after `folio_put(folio);`.
intent_record.how: This ensures that when the folio no longer matches `page_folio(page)`, the MM accounting for the huge PMD-sized folio is decremented before exiting, just as in the normal exit path. At runtime, it prevents this early-return path from skipping the counter update and leaving memory usage statistics inconsistent.

grouping_result.intent: Fix an early-exit path in huge PMD splitting to decrement MM counters before releasing the folio and returning.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets the huge PMD split early-exit path implicated in the bug, ensuring MM counters are updated before folio_put(), which prevents accessing folio state after its last reference is dropped.

candidates.rationale: This statement accesses folio state via mm_counter_file(folio) after the folio's last reference may already have been dropped by folio_put(), directly causing the use-after-free described in the root cause.
This releases the folio reference before the subsequent mm_counter_file(folio) call, enabling the folio to be freed and making the later access a use-after-free.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement dereferences folio state through mm_counter_file(folio) after the preceding folio_put(folio) may have dropped the last reference and freed the folio, matching the described use-after-free root cause.
